en.title: Brass Pendulum
en.subtitle: Blender · Refined native animation and guided spatial denoising
en.summary: Native geometry refinements shape the brass hoop and porcelain pendulum; the 42-to-44 mm lens keeps the whole plinth framed. The higher-resolution candidate uses real Albedo/Normal guides for per-frame spatial denoising, containing 144 frames at 24000/1001 fps over 6.006 seconds without audio. The older low-sample temporal experiment is preserved separately.
en.evidence_label: Native Cycles render · Real guide passes · Spatial OIDN
en.evidence_scope: Genuine DCC-MCP edits and save/reopen; native multilayer linear EXR at 960 × 720 and 96 samples passes through the unified dcc-media-enhance CLI, Blender compositor OIDN and explicit AgX/sRGB-to-BT.709 delivery. English/Chinese desktop/touch full-picture playback passed on recorded commit 5080041; later commits require separate checks.
limitations: This is an original procedural animation, not CineRecon reconstruction, a physical pendulum simulation, a benchmark or a model-quality score.
OIDN runs independently per frame here and is spatial; there is no temporal algorithm or motion compensation, and still-frame success does not prove motion stability.
The historical atadenoise experiment differs in geometry, camera, dimensions and sampling; its old raw video is not a same-source control for the new film.
MP4 is a lossy display encode. Browser references are independently decoded from that final MP4 and verify display consistency, not native EXR or high-sample quality ground truth.
The public native copy differs from production bytes; equivalence is limited to inspected settings and projected bounds, without pixel-identical rerender proof.

Touch is Chromium viewport emulation. Normal inline native controls can obscure the ended image; its separate real-fullscreen inspection does not claim unobstructed inline pixels. Physical devices, Safari/Firefox and production hosting were not tested.
No independently verifiable accepted task-configuration record establishes model or reasoning effort; every stage remains Unknown.
dcc-media-enhance source is MIT-licensed; original case assets remain rights-reserved, and upstream Blender, OIDN and FFmpeg licensing obligations remain unchanged.
en.alt: Brass hoop, porcelain pendulum and complete deep-teal plinth in the new candidate, from the actual 960 × 720 native render

en.title: Weathered Wooden Crate
en.subtitle: From a Designer material graph to Blender lookdev
en.summary: Separate wood grain, peeling paint, rust and scratches into editable material graphs, then realize thickness, fractures, fibers and contact shadows in a reopenable crate scene. The final lookdev combines 178 crate meshes, two Designer graphs and 13 packed textures.
en.evidence_label: Historical artwork · New camera attempt is partial stage evidence
en.evidence_scope: The 2026-10-12 camera attempt did not meet this pass’s target. The pinned historical source was actually reopened, two new camera scenes were saved/reopened, and 55 wide frames completed; only the first 50 frames, approximately 2.083 seconds, are delivered as a real excerpt. The planned six-second, 144-frame film is incomplete. Repeated host exits with status -9 ended rendering retries; their cause is unestablished. Successful excerpt decoding is not final-quality approval of the full film. The original model, Designer graphs, historical artwork and unknown production attribution remain intact.
limitations: This pass delivers only a 50-frame stage excerpt, not a high-quality finished film. Source scenes and the 55-frame checkpoint are retained. Host-exit causes are unestablished; quality reduction, interpolation and repeated still holds were not used to fill the missing duration.

The 2026-10-01 curation did not reproduce the work in a DCC. The 2026-10-12 pass actually reopened the source and attempted camera animation, without rebuilding the original model, Designer graphs or SBS materials. The film target remains incomplete.
The original prompt, complete MCP tool-call logs and adapter/core versions are not public.
The historical reference image was produced through Codex image generation. It is a reference input, not a deliverable made through DCC-MCP.
Dimensions, weathering and damage are artistic estimates; edge wear comes from the Designer board distribution, not a curvature bake.
This is a dense lookdev scene with tiling/overlapping UVs, not game-ready topology or a unique baked atlas.
The source records claim only that files can be reopened and recomputed, not that recomputed PNG bytes are identical.

The source repository declares MIT for the repository as a whole; no separate licenses are listed for the artwork, generated reference image or materials. Adobe built-in library assets are referenced only through sbs:// and are not distributed on this site.

The public excerpt uses original frames 1–50; extra checkpoint frames 51–55 use two OIDN threads. Same-frame calibration differs by at most 2/255 per channel, is not pixel-identical, and does not prove reduced peak memory. The old ZIP remains historical; the new cameras are rebuilt from the pinned input and recipe.

Public evidence is a curated, redacted projection of actual calls, not the complete original logs.

120 action images play at a 12fps cadence; no claim is made of 24fps independent motion frames or soundtrack design.
Early JPEG white-frame, gantry and projected-bounding-box failures are retained in the evidence; the final film uses verified PNG inputs.
The before/after development comparison rerenders an early geometry/material version at the final wagon spacing and camera pose, as explicitly labeled.

The final project passed acceptance for native controls, saving a copy with unchanged parameters and reopening. Parameter edits/parameter Undo and cross-environment pixel identity are outside this scope.
The compact package can open CAD/Blender independently; Kdenlive requires the 122 PNGs in the full package. The full package passed login-free download and SHA-256 verification.
Public evidence is a curated projection of actual tool calls; complete private logs, software runtimes and font files are not distributed with the package.
The added soundtrack does not mean that the original visual project was remade. No subjective listening review is recorded, and no integration verification with a private game project is included.

en.title: Dawnkeep · Oath of the Last Light

en.summary: Play Elyra, the Dawnwarden, and protect the Dawnheart in a floating woodland. Intercept enemies, upgrade equipment, cast Q/E/R abilities and build supporting towers through eight waves and the Crownless King. Includes native English/Chinese UI, browser play and an editable Godot project.
en.evidence_label: Actual typed MCP authoring · Native and Web eight-wave victories
en.evidence_scope: Frozen revision 957c1d3: Godot typed MCP created, saved and reopened the native scene. Actual X11 keyboard/mouse and desktop Chrome independently completed eight-wave victory, natural wave-five defeat and restarts. Portrait uses emulated touch, not a physical phone. Original meshes were authored with native Blender Python, not Blender MCP; the public film is actual native screen capture.
limitations: Subjective music listening, physical phones, multitouch, physical GPU performance and native OS-window closing remain untested.
Automated actual-input tests establish the recorded strategies and win/loss paths, not balance or compatibility across every strategy, browser or device.
The excerpt has explicit time edits and is not a continuous full-campaign film; recording measurements and full decoding do not replace listening.
The browser playable is the actual single-thread Godot Compatibility export. The game initially uses Chinese; press L or click EN for English. It does not automatically inherit the page language.
The native ZIP requires Godot 4.6.3 and contains an editable project rather than a standalone executable. Downloading or playing grants no additional license to the original work.
Full-game CI and public-site deployment are separate stages; the 957c1d3 record alone does not establish deployed network, page or playback behavior.
